paper_title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

Introduction Figure 2. Downstream accuracy averaged over 10 tasks. Transformers solve tasks by composing attention heads across layers into circuits (Elhage et al., 2020; Olsson et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023; Merullo et al., 2024): an earlier head writes feature into subspace of the residual stream, and later head reads from that subspace into its query, key or value. Induction heads, for example, read the output of previous-token head through their keys (K-composition) (Olsson et al., 2022). is fixed: head cannot choose which heads to read from. model that needs different circuits for different inputs therefore keeps all of them wired at once, lets them compete for the residual stream, and can gate them only indirectly, e.g., by sending heads attention to sink token (Xiao et al., 2024b). We ask whether the wiring itself can be chosen per token, i.e., whether circuits can be made rewirable. The composition between two heads, however, is determined by the product of their output and input projections, virtual weight that does not change after training (Elhage et al., 2020). Attention makes the horizontal flow of information across tokens input-dependent: head chooses which tokens to attend to. In contrast, the vertical flow across layers Recent work has enriched the vertical flow. Dense connections let layer aggregate the outputs of all earlier layers (Pagliardini et al., 2024); MUDDFormer (Xiao et al., 2025) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes) (Kimi Team, 2026a) make this aggregation input-dependent, turning it into depth-wise (i.e., vertical) attention (separate for the query, 1 Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention key, value and residual inputs in MUDDFormer); and HyperConnections (HC) (Zhu et al., 2025) and its manifoldconstrained variant mHC (Xie et al., 2025) maintain several residual streams with learnable or dynamic mixing. In all of them, however, the vertical channel meets horizontal attention only through the hidden state of layer, in which the outputs of all heads have already been summed and mixed together: head can neither single out particular earlier head nor be singled out by later one. The vertical and horizontal flows run side by side, never woven together. To make circuits rewirable, we propose loom attention, in which head chooses which earlier heads to read from just as it chooses which tokens to attend to. By attending vertically over the outputs of these heads at the same token, the head obtains its query, key and value to perform the standard horizontal attention over tokens, and its output is in turn attended to vertically by later heads. Vertical and horizontal attention are thus interwoven, each feeding the other at every head, like the warp and weft of loom (Figure 1). Naive vertical attention over the outputs of all earlier heads is, however, expensive. We therefore instantiate it with normalized and gated linear attention over per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as second residual stream. We call the resulting dual-stream architecture LoomFormer, after drawlooma loom in which separate stored pattern selects which warp threads to lift at each pick, rather than repeating one fixed pattern. 1 Here the ordinary vector stream plays the pattern, carrying controlwhich memory slots each head writes and reads (weaving different circuit per token) as well as which tokens to attend towhile the matrix stream carries the content moved across tokens. The two streams are coupled through attention outputs and FFN writes. Extensive experiments on language modeling and downstream tasks across model sizes and training token budgets show that LoomFormer adds only 2.03.7% FLOPs while matching Transformers trained with over 3 compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, 1.72.8. Extended Related Work Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention Cross-layer connections and residual-stream architectures. Beyond standard residual connections (He et al., 2016), early work strengthened depth-wise signal propagation through input-dependent gating in Highway Networks (Srivastava et al., 2015) and all-to-all layer aggregation with static or learnable weights in DenseNet (Huang et al., 2017), DLCL (Wang et al., 2019) and DenseFormer (Pagliardini et al., 2024). Subsequent architectures introduced cross-layer attention over earlier layer representations (ElNokrashy et al., 2022; Fang et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024; Kimi Team, 2026a), multi-stream residual states with dynamic or manifold-constrained mixing in HC and mHC (Zhu et al., 2025; Xie et al., 2025), and decoupled Q/K/V/residual layer aggregation in MUDDFormer (Xiao et al., 2025). As analyzed in Section 4 and Section A.7, all of these mechanisms operate at the granularity of whole layers (or layer Q/K/V), summing the outputs of all heads within layer before routing and restricting the within-token wiring rank to 1 (or 3). The Residual Matrix Transformer (RMT) (Mak & Flanigan, 2025) replaces the vector residual stream entirely with pure matrix residual stream, which heads and FFNs read and write through static key vectors so the stream can be widened cheaply. LoomFormer instead keeps dual-stream architecture that separates control on the vector stream from content on the matrix stream: the compact vector stream generates per-token ports cheaply, whereas RMTs static ports fall under Theorem 3.1(i) and remain node-gated however wide the matrix is made (4D in RMTs main configuration vs. 2D + in LoomFormer). Cross-layer token attention and KV sharing. OmniNet (Tay et al., 2021) lets every token attend directly to all tokens across all layers, incurring attention cost quadratic in LT ; loom attention instead factors cross-layer routing within each token through fixed-size matrix memory in O(LT Ddk) time and composes it with standard within-layer horizontal attention. Cross-Layer Attention (CLA) (Brandon et al., 2024) shares key-value caches across adjacent layers to reduce inference memory at modest quality trade-off, whereas loom attention dynamically composes earlier head outputs into distinct per-head queries, keys and values at every layer (Section 5.3). Mechanistic interpretability and intra-layer advances. Circuit-level interpretability studies (Elhage et al., 2020; Olsson et al., 2022; Conmy et al., 2023; Hanna et al., 2024; Merullo et al., 2024; Ni et al., 2025) show that Transformers implement tasks by composing specific upstream and downstream heads across layers; loom attention turns this implicit, static composition into an explicit, per-token operation over . Orthogonal intra-layer advancesincluding improved horizontal attention (Liu et al., 2024; Xiao et al., 2024a; Ye et al., 2024; Leviathan et al., 2024), sequence-axis linear attention and state-space models (Gu & Dao, 2024; Dao & Gu, 2024; Peng et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2024b; 2025), and sparse Mixture-of-Experts FFNs (Fedus et al., 2022; Dai et al., 2024)modify horizontal mixing or FFN capacity within layer and can be combined directly with loom attention along depth.
